newsitem.title: UK: Lurch to right would doom UK Conservatives-Brittan.
newsitem.headline: Lurch to right would doom UK Conservatives-Brittan.

text.p: European Union commissioner Sir Leon Brittan on Thursday warned Britain's Conservatives against "a lurch to the right" following their humiliating May 1 election defeat.
"It would be a great mistake to seek in vain to regain popularity by adopting the anti-European approach again," Brittan, a former Conservative cabinet minister, said.
His remarks were contained in a statement which he will make to political journalists in London on Friday, the text of which he released in advance.

The Conservatives were reduced to a rump of 165 MPs, barely a quarter of the House of Commons, at the election, which followed a lengthy period of internal party strife over issues such as the single European currency.
Now the party is in the middle of a campaign in which six former cabinet ministers, some of them with impeccable right-wing credentials, are scrapping to replace John Major as Conservative leader.

"The Conservative Party should not and need not tear itself apart on the issue of Europe," Brittan said. "The last election showed that the Eurosceptic stance was not exactly a winning streak, to put it mildly."
He said next month's EU Intergovernmental Conference (IGC) was "extremely unlikely" to usher in radical changes to the way the bloc was run.
Brittan said that the other major issue due for decision in the EU -- the single currency -- would look very different by the time of the next election, probably in more than four years time.
